findings.finding: ADDW/SUBW opcode definitions (MATCH_ADDW=0x3b, MATCH_SUBW=0x4000003b) are RV64I base ISA instructions for 32-bit word arithmetic with sign extension, not P-ext double-wide scalar add/subtract. The '+W' suffix denotes 32-bit word operations in RV64I per rv64.adoc §Integer Computational Instructions, not P-ext functionality.

spec_citations.excerpt: Additional instruction variants are provided to manipulate 32-bit values in RV64I, indicated by a 'W' suffix to the opcode. These 'W' instructions ignore the upper 32 bits of their inputs and always produce 32-bit signed values, sign-extending them to 64 bits.

findings.finding: No P-extension (Zpn, Zpsfoperand) double-wide scalar add/subtract instruction definitions exist in encoding.h. The RISC-V P-extension (packed SIMD) is described in zp.adoc as a placeholder for forthcoming extensions and has not been ratified. FreeBSD does not implement any P-ext instructions because there is no ratified spec.

findings.finding: Disassembly table entries for addw/subw correspond to RV64I base ISA instructions, not P-ext double-wide scalar operations. These correctly use MATCH_ADDW/MASK_ADDW and MATCH_SUBW/MASK_SUBW from encoding.h.

spec_citations.excerpt: ADDW and SUBW are RV64I-only instructions that are defined analogously to ADD and SUB but operate on 32-bit values and produce signed 32-bit results. Overflows are ignored, and the low 32-bits of the result is sign-extended to 64 bits.
